Hajdunanas Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Polgári út 6501/5, Hungary

Not demolished. Hajdúnánás was the oldest and most populous Jewish settlement among its neighboring towns, with the first Jew permitted to lease a tavern there in 1786; wealthy merchant Dávid Fried helped fund the first synagogue in 1825, dedicated by the noted rabbi of Nagykálló, Eizik Taub. Rabbi Israel Efraim Fischl, one of the last pupils of the Chatam Sofer, led the community from 1862 until his death in 1898, overseeing the founding of a Jewish primary school in 1877 and charitable societies in the 1880s. The community reached about 700 individuals across 160 families by the early 20th century, growing to 1,080 by 1940. Following the German occupation in March 1944, a ghetto was established that May, and the town's Jews were deported that June to Strasshof, Mauthausen, and Auschwitz.
